text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in NOrwegian papers this morning:

- The ombudsman for children wants all public employees working with youngsters to be issued with a police certificate to prove that they have not been convicted of any crimes concerning the abuse of children.
- Trondheim soccer club Rosenborg meet AC Milan in Milan on Wednesday night in the last match of the qualifying round in the European Champion's League.

- Analysts say oil company Saga Petroleum ASA is paying an extremely high price for British-based Santa Fe Exploration Ltd. At the beginning of the year consultants Arthur Andersen estimated Santa Fe to be worth around 3.9 billion crowns, almost the half of price Saga is expected to pay for ther North Sea exploration group.

- Industrial group Norsk Hydro ASA held a presentation for analysts on Tuesday. President and Chief Executive Officer Egil Myklebust said Hydro will double its turnover by 2005. Myklebust wants a return on locked-up capital of 15 percent.
- The Guatemalan government and leftist rebels meet in Oslo Wednesday to sign the first of several peace agreements to put an end to 36 years of bloody civil war.
